info.title: Advertising
info.description: Search Engine Marketing (SEM) allows you to promote your listings through Google Shopping Ads and reach customers who are searching on Google for products like yours.

get.description: This API allows you to retrieve detailed information about a specific campaign. Provide the campaign's unique ID in the request to fetch its attributes.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Campaign ID of the campaign whose details are to be retrieved.

put.description: This API allows you to modify an existing campaign's details and manage its associated items. You must provide the campaign's unique ID along with the necessary changes in the request. The specified updates will be applied while preserving the campaign's unique identifier.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Campaign ID of the campaign to be updated.

delete.description: This API allows you to permanently remove an existing campaign from the system. Once deleted, the campaign and its unique ID will no longer be retrievable. The campaign's unique ID must be included in the request.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Campaign ID of the campaign to be deleted.

put.description: This API allows you to stop an active campaign. Stopping a campaign does not delete it but prevents further actions. The campaign's unique ID must be included in the request.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Campaign ID of the campaign to be stopped.

post.description:
Search for item-level diagnostic issues that block or limit items from being used in Search Engine Marketing (SEM). Returns paginated, item-level diagnostic details including campaign associations, issue types, severity, remediation guidance, and overall item status.
Market availability: US only Items in SEM campaigns must meet content, quality, and policy requirements before they can be advertised on search engines (For example, Google Shopping Ads). This endpoint surfaces the specific issues preventing or limiting an item's SEM eligibility, along with actionable remediation guidance so sellers can resolve problems and restore advertising reach. ### Current scope This endpoint currently returns diagnostics for **items that are part of active SEM campaigns** for the authenticated seller. Each item in the response includes its `campaignAssociations` — the list of campaigns the item belongs to. Items not associated with any campaign are not included in the results. ### Default behavior - When no request body is provided, defaults to `offset=0`, `limit=100` with no filters - When no `issueCategory` filter is provided, returns **only items with issues** (`BLOCKED` or `LIMITED`) - To include healthy items, explicitly pass `issueCategory` filter with `NO_ISSUES` or all three values - By default, the API prioritizes returning actionable diagnostic issues rather than healthy items. This reduces payload size and improves relevance ### Supported filters Filters are combined with AND logic. Multiple values within a single filter act as OR. | Filter Field | Supported Values | Max Values | Description | |-----------------|-------------------------------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------| | `issues` | Any valid `issueType` enum value | 100 | Filter by specific SEM issue types (For example, `ITEM_OUT_OF_STOCK`, `TITLE_TOO_LONG`, `POLICY_VIOLATION`) | | `issueCategory` | `LIMITED`, `BLOCKED`, `NO_ISSUES` | 100 | Filter by SEM issue severity — `BLOCKED` items cannot be advertised at all, `LIMITED` items have reduced SEM performance | | `itemId` | Numeric string item IDs | 100 | Filter by Walmart catalog item identifiers within the seller's active campaigns. *In a future release, this filter will also support items outside of campaigns.* | ### Response structure Each response contains two top-level fields: - `pagination`: Standard pagination metadata including `hasNextPage`/`hasPreviousPage` for convenient UI navigation - `data`: Array of item-level diagnostics. Each item appears **once** per unique `offerId` with all campaign associations listed. Each item includes an `issueCategory` field representing the overall SEM eligibility status of the item, and an `issues` array containing issue type identifiers. Issues are item-level, not campaign-specific — a blocked item is blocked in all SEM campaigns it belongs to. Issue metadata (name, description, fixability, help links) is not included in this response. Partners should use the dedicated `GET /item-issues/issue-types` endpoint to retrieve complete issue metadata and cache it locally (TTL: 24 hours). ### Issue categories | Category | SEM Impact | |--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `BLOCKED` | Item **cannot be advertised** on search engines. Must be resolved before the item can appear in SEM ads. Examples: out of stock, missing title, policy violation, invalid image. | | `LIMITED` | Item **can be advertised but with reduced visibility** or performance on search engines. Resolving these issues improves ad reach and effectiveness. Examples: title too long, low image quality, description too short. | | `NO_ISSUES` | Item has no SEM issues and can be advertised normally with full visibility. | ### Actionable vs non-actionable issues Each issue type has an `isFixable` flag available via the `GET /item-issues/issue-types` reference endpoint: - `isFixable=true`: Seller can fix the issue to restore SEM eligibility (For example, restock inventory, update title, fix image). Partners should surface these with a "Fix Now" UI affordance. - `isFixable=false`: Requires Walmart or system intervention (For example, Google policy violations). Partners should display these as informational — the seller cannot directly resolve them.

Optional search request with pagination and filters.
Defaults to `offset=0`, `limit=100` with no filters if body is absent.
When no `issueCategory` filter is provided, only items with issues (`BLOCKED` or `LIMITED`) are returned.

To include all items, explicitly pass `issueCategory` filter with all three values: `LIMITED`, `BLOCKED`, `NO_ISSUES`.

get.description:
Returns the complete, authoritative metadata for all SEM eligibility issue types (~61 issue types, ~5KB).
Market availability: US only Items used in Search Engine Marketing (SEM) campaigns such as Google Shopping Ads must meet specific content, quality, and policy requirements before they can be advertised on search engines. When items fail to meet these requirements, they are flagged with specific issue types that either **block** the item from being advertised entirely or **limit** its visibility and performance in SEM. This endpoint returns the complete catalog of all issue types that can affect an item's SEM eligibility, along with human-readable names, descriptions, remediation guidance, severity categories, and help links. It serves as the **single source of truth** for issue metadata. ### Current scope The issue types returned by this endpoint apply to items that are currently part of active SEM campaigns. The `POST /item-issues/search` endpoint uses these issue types to report diagnostics on campaign items. ### Future extensibility In a future release, the `POST /item-issues/search` endpoint will support querying diagnostic issues for any item in the seller's catalog — even items not yet added to a campaign — using the `itemId` filter. The same issue types returned by this endpoint will apply to those items as well, enabling sellers to proactively diagnose and fix issues before campaign onboarding. ### SEM eligibility issue categories Each issue type belongs to one of three categories that indicate its impact on an item's ability to be advertised on search engines: | Category | Count | SEM Impact | |--------------|-------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `BLOCKED` | ~49 | Item **cannot be advertised** on search engines. Must be resolved before the item can appear in SEM ads. Examples: `ITEM_OUT_OF_STOCK`, `POLICY_VIOLATION`, `MISSING_INVALID_TITLE`, `INVALID_IMAGE`, `BUYBOX_NOT_WINNER` | | `LIMITED` | ~11 | Item **can be advertised but with reduced visibility** or performance on search engines. Resolving these issues improves ad reach and effectiveness. Examples: `TITLE_TOO_LONG`, `LOW_IMAGE_QUALITY`, `DESCRIPTION_TOO_SHORT`, `LOW_OFFER_LISTING_QUALITY` | | `NO_ISSUES` | ~1 | Informational statuses such as `DUPLICATE_OFFER` — item has no SEM eligibility issues | ### Actionable vs non-actionable issues Each issue type includes an `isFixable` flag that indicates whether the seller can resolve the issue: - `isFixable=true`: Seller can take action to restore or improve SEM eligibility (For example, restock inventory, update title, improve image quality). Partners should surface these with a "Fix Now" UI affordance. - `isFixable=false`: Requires Walmart or system intervention (For example, Google policy violations, BuyBox eligibility). Partners should display these as informational — the seller cannot directly resolve them. ### Response structure The response is a map keyed by `issueType` (string), where each value is an `IssueMetadata` object containing: - `issueName`: Human-readable short headline for UI display (For example, "Item Out of Stock") - `issueCategory`: SEM eligibility impact — `BLOCKED` (cannot advertise on search engines) or `LIMITED` (reduced SEM visibility) - `isFixable`: Whether the partner can remediate this issue to restore SEM eligibility - `issueDescription`: Human-readable description with specific remediation guidance (For example, "Item is out of stock. Add inventory to make the item available.") - `learnMoreUrl`: Help link to Walmart-hosted or Google support documentation for step-by-step remediation. May be null for some issue types. ### Recommended usage pattern 1. Call this endpoint **once** on application initialization 2. Cache the result locally (recommended **TTL: 24 hours**) 3. Use cached metadata to enrich items returned by the `POST /item-issues/search` endpoint — match each item's `issueType` to the cached metadata for display name, description, and help links 4. Use `isFixable` to drive UI affordances: show "Fix Now" buttons for fixable SEM issues, informational badges for non-fixable ones 5. Use `learnMoreUrl` to deep-link to help documentation for step-by-step remediation guidance 6. Use `issueCategory` to color-code or badge issues in your UI: red for `BLOCKED` (cannot advertise), yellow for `LIMITED` (reduced SEM performance).

post.description:
Search for campaign-level recommendations to improve SEM campaign performance. Returns a paginated list of active campaigns for the authenticated seller, each enriched with actionable recommendations — including budget adjustments and bidding strategy optimizations — along with projected performance impact metrics (clicks, impressions, ad spend).
Market availability: US only ### Why this API matters SEM campaigns require continuous optimization to stay competitive. Budget constraints and suboptimal bidding strategies are the two most common reasons campaigns underperform. Without data-driven guidance, sellers either overspend without results or miss revenue opportunities by underspending. This API bridges that gap by surfacing **machine-generated recommendations** for each active campaign, complete with projected impact on clicks, impressions, and ad spend. Partners can integrate these recommendations into their dashboards and automation pipelines to: - **Increase ROAS**: Apply budget and bidding strategy recommendations to maximize return on ad spend - **Reduce wasted spend**: Identify campaigns where budget is being underutilized or misallocated - **Automate campaign tuning**: Build automated workflows that periodically fetch recommendations and apply them programmatically, reducing manual effort and reaction time - **Enable data-driven decisions**: Each recommendation includes three impact scenarios (recommended, conservative, aggressive) so sellers can choose the option that fits their risk tolerance ### Key use cases 1. **Campaign Health Dashboard**: Display campaigns with pending recommendations, color-coded by type (`BUDGET` vs `BIDDING_STRATEGY`), with projected impact metrics 2. **Automated Budget Optimizer**: Periodically poll this API and auto-apply budget recommendations that meet a minimum projected ROAS threshold 3. **Bidding Strategy Advisor**: Surface bidding strategy change suggestions to sellers with before/after performance projections 4. **Bulk Campaign Management**: Retrieve all recommendations across campaigns in a single paginated call, enabling batch review and bulk application of changes ### How it works The API returns only active campaigns that are eligible for recommendations. You can filter results using `campaignIds` or `recommendationType` (`BUDGET` or `BIDDING_STRATEGY`). ### Default behavior - When no request body is provided, the API defaults to `offset=0`, `limit=10`. - By default, the API returns recommendations for both `BUDGET` and `BIDDING_STRATEGY`. - Results are not sorted by default; use the sort object to order by adspend. - Returns only **active campaigns** that have at least one pending recommendation - Results are not sorted by default; use the `sort` object to order by `adspend` ### Supported filters Filters are combined with AND logic. Multiple values within a single filter act as OR. | Filter Field | Supported Values | Description | |---------------------------|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------| | `campaignIds` | Numeric string campaign IDs | Filter by specific campaign identifiers | | `recommendationType` | `BUDGET`, `BIDDING_STRATEGY` | Filter by recommendation type | ### Sorting Results can be sorted using the `sort` object: | Sort Field | Supported Orders | Description | |------------|------------------|------------------------------------------| | `adspend` | `ASC`, `DESC` | Sort campaigns by ad spend | ### Recommendation types | Type | Description | |--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `BUDGET` | Recommended total or daily budget adjustment to improve campaign reach | | `BIDDING_STRATEGY` | Recommended change to bidding strategy for better performance | ### Response structure Each response contains two top-level fields: - `pagination`: Standard pagination metadata (`pageNo`, `pageSize`, `totalCount`, `totalPages`, `hasNextPage`, `hasPreviousPage`) - `data`: Array of campaign-level suggestions. Each campaign includes current settings (bidding strategy, target ROAS, daily budget) and an array of `campaignRecommendations` with projected performance impact at three levels: recommended, minimum, and maximum. ### Performance impact projections Each recommendation includes a `recommendedValueImpact` object with up to three scenarios: - **recommended**: The optimal suggested value (marked `isRecommended: true`) - **minRecommendation**: A conservative lower-bound option (may be `null` if not applicable) - **maxRecommendation**: An aggressive upper-bound option

ItemDiagnosticSearchRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching item-level diagnostics.

All fields are optional. The request body itself is also optional — when absent, sensible defaults are applied:
- `page.offset`: 0
- `page.limit`: 100
- No filters (returns only items with issues: `BLOCKED` or `LIMITED`)

**Current scope**: Results are scoped to items in active SEM campaigns. In a future release, the `itemId` filter will support querying any item in the seller's catalog.

**Default behavior**: When no `issueCategory` filter is provided, the API returns **only items with issues** (`BLOCKED` or `LIMITED`). This design decision ensures diagnostics consumers receive actionable problems first, reducing payload size and improving relevance. To include healthy items, explicitly pass `issueCategory` with value `NO_ISSUES` or use all three values.

**Filter behavior**: Filters are combined with AND logic. Multiple values within a single filter act as OR. For example, filtering by `issueCategory`=[`BLOCKED`, `LIMITED`] returns items that are either `BLOCKED` or `LIMITED`. Adding a second filter `issues`=[`ITEM_OUT_OF_STOCK`] narrows results to items that are (`BLOCKED` or `LIMITED`) AND have `ITEM_OUT_OF_STOCK`.

filters.description:
List of filters to narrow down results.
Multiple filters are combined using the AND operator.
Each filter field must be specified only once (no duplicates).

DiagnosticPage.description:
Pagination configuration for controlling result set size and navigation.

**Defaults when page is not provided**: offset=0, limit=100

Both `offset` and `limit` are required when the `page` object is provided.

offset.description:
The starting position for fetching records (0-based).

**Constraints**: Must be zero or a positive value
**Default**: 0 (when page is not provided).

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to fetch per page.

**Constraints**: Must be between 1 and 100
**Default**: 100 (when page is not provided).

ItemDiagnosticFilter.description:
Filter configuration to narrow down item diagnostic results.

**Validation Rules**:
- Both `field` and `values` are required when a filter is provided
- Each filter field must be specified only once (no duplicate fields)
- Each filter field supports a maximum of 100 values
- Filter values are case-insensitive
- Multiple values within a filter act as an OR condition
- Multiple filters are combined with AND logic

field.description:
Field by which the filtering is to be done.

**Supported fields**:
- `issues`: Filter by specific issue types (For example, `ITEM_OUT_OF_STOCK`, `TITLE_TOO_LONG`)
- `issueCategory`: Filter by issue severity category (`LIMITED`, `BLOCKED`, `NO_ISSUES`)
- `itemId`: Filter by Walmart item IDs (numeric strings). Currently filters within items in active SEM campaigns. *In a future release, this will also support items not yet associated with any campaign.*

values.description:
List of values for the specified field.
Multiple values act as an OR condition within the filter.

**Constraints**: At least 1 value required, maximum 100 values per filter.

**Valid values by field**:
- `issues`: Any valid `issueType` enum value (Refer to the issue types endpoint)
- `issueCategory`: `LIMITED`, `BLOCKED`, `NO_ISSUES`
- `itemId`: Numeric string item IDs (currently scoped to items in active SEM campaigns)

ItemDiagnosticSearchResponse.description:
Search response containing paginated item-level diagnostics and pagination metadata.

Each item's `issues` array contains `issueType` values as lightweight lookup keys.
Partners should use the dedicated `GET /item-issues/issue-types` endpoint to retrieve
complete issue metadata (name, description, category, fixability, help links) and cache
it locally (recommended TTL: 24 hours) to enrich search results.

data.description:
Paginated list of item-level diagnostics.
Each item appears once per unique `offerId` with all campaign associations.
Empty array when no items match the search criteria.

ActiveItemIssues.description:
Item-level diagnostic data including product details, campaign associations, overall item status, and list of issues.

Each `ActiveItemIssues` object appears **once** per unique `offerId`.
The `campaignAssociations` array lists all campaigns the item belongs to.
Issues are **item-level**, not campaign-specific — the same issue applies regardless of which campaign the item is in.

### Identifier Contract
| Field     | Source           | Format                  | Description                                                              |
|-----------|------------------|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `offerId` | Walmart-assigned | String                  | Uniquely identifies a specific offer (item + seller). Recommended primary key for partner systems. |
| `itemId`  | Walmart-assigned | Numeric string          | Walmart catalog item identifier. Shared across sellers offering the same product. |
| `sku`     | Partner-assigned | Alphanumeric (partner-defined) | The partner's own SKU. Never a Walmart-assigned value.               |

offerId.description: Unique offer identifier. Enables deep-linking, correlation with partner inventory systems, and disambiguation of items across campaigns.

itemId.description:
Walmart catalog item identifier (numeric string).
Shared across sellers offering the same product.

sku.description:
Partner-assigned Stock Keeping Unit.
Always the partner's own SKU, never a Walmart-assigned value.

campaignAssociations.description:
List of all campaigns this item is associated with.
A single item may participate in multiple campaigns.

issueCategory.description:
Overall SEM eligibility status derived from all issues affecting this item.

- **NO_ISSUES**: Item has no SEM issues and can be advertised on search engines with full visibility
- **LIMITED**: Item has issues that reduce its visibility or performance in Search Engine Marketing
- **BLOCKED**: Item has critical issues that completely prevent it from being advertised on search engines

issues.description:
List of issues affecting this item.
Each issue contains an `issueType` that can be used as a lookup key
into the issue metadata returned by the `GET /item-issues/issue-types` endpoint.
Empty array when item has no issues.

CampaignRef.description:
Campaign association reference. Represents a campaign that an item belongs to.
A single item can appear in multiple campaigns.

Issue.description:
Issue affecting an item. Contains the issue type identifier only.

The `issueType` serves as a lookup key into the issue metadata returned by the `GET /item-issues/issue-types` reference endpoint. All static metadata (name, description, category, fixability, help links) lives in that endpoint's response.

issueType.description: Lookup key into the issue metadata returned by the `GET /item-issues/issue-types` endpoint. Maps to one of the supported issue type enum values.

IssueMetadata.description:
Static metadata for an issue type. Provides human-readable information for building diagnostic UIs including issue name, description, severity, remediability, and help links.

This metadata is the same for every item — it describes the issue type itself, not a specific occurrence on an item.

issueName.description: Human-readable issue name for UI short headline display.

issueCategory.description:
Issue severity category.

- **BLOCKED**: Item cannot be advertised
- **LIMITED**: Item has reduced visibility or performance
- **NO_ISSUES**: Item has no SEM eligibility issues

isFixable.description:
Whether the partner can remediate this issue.
`true` = actionable by partner (show "Fix Now" UI affordance),
`false` = requires Walmart or system intervention (informational only).

issueDescription.description: Human-readable description of the issue with remediation guidance.
issueDescription.example: Item is out of stock. Add inventory to make the item available.

learnMoreUrl.description:
Help link (Walmart-hosted or Google support) for additional information.
May be null if no help link is available for this issue type.

IssueTypesResponse.description:
Complete map of all supported issue types keyed by issue type name.
Contains metadata for all 61 issue types.
Partners should cache this response (TTL: 24 hours) and use it as the authoritative source for issue metadata.

DiagnosticPagination.description:
Pagination metadata for navigating through search results.

Includes `hasNextPage` and `hasPreviousPage` boolean flags for
convenient pagination control in UIs.

pageNo.description:
Current page number (0-based).
Calculated as: offset / limit

pageSize.description: Number of items per page (same as `limit` in request).

totalCount.description: Total number of items matching the search criteria across all pages.

totalPages.description:
Total number of pages available.
Calculated as: ceil(totalCount / pageSize).

hasNextPage.description: `true` if more pages exist after the current page.

hasPreviousPage.description: `true` if pages exist before the current page.

ErrorResponse.description:
Standardized error response envelope containing an array of error details.
All error responses from the API follow this structure.

error.description: List of error details. Typically contains a single error, but may contain multiple errors for validation failures.

ErrorDetail.description: Error detail following RFC 7807 (Problem Details for HTTP APIs).

type.description: A URI reference that identifies the problem type.

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

status.description: The HTTP status code generated by the origin server for this occurrence of the problem.

detail.description: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the problem.

instance.description: A URI reference that identifies the specific occurrence of the problem.

ErrorResponse429.description: Error response envelope for rate limit (429) errors returned by the API Gateway.

error.description: List of rate limit error details.

ErrorDetail429.description:
Rate limit error detail following RFC 7807 (Problem Details for HTTP APIs).
Returned by the API Gateway when the request threshold is violated.

type.description: A URI reference that identifies the problem type.

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

status.description: The HTTP status code generated by the origin server for this occurrence of the problem.

detail.description: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the problem.
detail.example: You have exceeded your API calls threshold. Check your seller account documentation to find out how many API calls are allowed for your account.

instance.description: A URI reference that identifies the specific occurrence of the problem.

CampaignRecommendationsSearchRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching campaign-level recommendations.

All fields are optional. The request body itself is also optional — when absent, sensible defaults are applied:
- `page.offset`: 0
- `page.limit`: 10
- No filters, no sorting

**Filter behavior**: Filters are combined with AND logic. Multiple values within a single filter act as OR.

filters.description:
List of filters to narrow down results.
Multiple filters are combined with AND logic.
Each filter field must be specified only once (no duplicates).

CampaignRecommendationsPage.description:
Pagination configuration for campaign recommendations.

**Defaults when page is not provided**: `offset=0`, `limit=10`

Both `offset` and `limit` are required when the `page` object is provided.

offset.description:
The starting position for fetching records (0-based).

**Constraints**: Must be zero or a positive value
**Default**: 0 (when page is not provided).

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to fetch per page.

**Constraints**: Must be between 1 and 100
**Default**: 10 (when page is not provided).

RecommendationsSort.description:
Sorting configuration for ordering search results.

Both `field` and `order` are required when the `sort` object is provided.

field.description: Field by which the results should be sorted.

CampaignRecommendationsFilter.description:
Filter configuration to narrow down campaign recommendation results.

**Validation Rules**:
- Both `field` and `values` are required when a filter is provided
- Each filter field must be specified only once (no duplicate fields)
- Filter values must contain at least one value
- Multiple values within a filter act as an OR condition
- Multiple filters are combined with AND logic.

field.description:
Field by which the filtering is to be done.

**Supported fields**:
- `campaignIds`: Filter by specific campaign identifiers
- `recommendationType`: Filter by recommendation type (`BUDGET`, `BIDDING_STRATEGY`).

values.description:
List of values for the specified field.
Multiple values act as an OR condition within the filter.

**Valid values by field**:
- `campaignIds`: Numeric string campaign IDs
- `recommendationType`: `BUDGET`, `BIDDING_STRATEGY`.

CampaignRecommendationsSearchResponse.description:
Search response containing paginated campaign-level recommendations and pagination metadata.

Each campaign in the `data` array includes its current settings (bidding strategy, target ROAS, daily budget) and an array of actionable recommendations with projected performance impact.

data.description:
Paginated list of campaign-level suggestions.
Each campaign appears once with all its recommendations.
Empty array when no campaigns match the search criteria.

CampaignSuggestion.description: Campaign-level suggestion containing current campaign settings and an array of actionable recommendations.

biddingStrategyType.description: Current bidding strategy type configured for the campaign (For example, `TARGET_ROAS`, `MAXIMIZE_CLICKS`).

targetRoas.description: Current target Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) configured for the campaign. Only applicable when `biddingStrategyType` is `TARGET_ROAS`.

dailyBudget.description: Current daily budget configured for the campaign (in USD).

campaignRecommendations.description:
List of actionable recommendations for this campaign.
Each recommendation includes the type, recommended value, and projected performance impact.

CampaignRecommendation.description: An actionable recommendation for a campaign. Includes the recommendation type, suggested value, and projected performance impact at three levels (recommended, minimum, maximum).

type.description:
Recommendation category.

- **BUDGET**: Recommended budget adjustment (daily or total)
- **BIDDING_STRATEGY**: Recommended change to bidding strategy

subType.description: Specific recommendation subtype indicating the optimization action being suggested. Example values include `INCREASE_DAILY_BUDGET` and bidding strategy adjustment actions.

recommendedValue.description: The primary recommended value as a string representation. For budget recommendations, this is the suggested new budget amount.

RecommendedValueImpact.description:
Projected performance impact of the recommendation at three levels.

- **recommended**: The optimal suggested value (marked `isRecommended: true`)
- **minRecommendation**: A conservative lower-bound option. May be `null` if not applicable.
- **maxRecommendation**: An aggressive upper-bound option. May be `null` if not applicable.

recommended.description: The optimal recommended option. Always present and marked with `isRecommended: true`.

minRecommendation.description: Conservative lower-bound recommendation option. May be `null` when a minimum option is not applicable.

maxRecommendation.description: Aggressive upper-bound recommendation option. May be `null` when a maximum option is not applicable.

ImpactOption.description: A single recommendation option with its projected performance impact.

value.description: The recommended value for this option (For example, suggested daily budget amount in USD).

adspendChange.description: Projected change in ad spend (in USD) if this option is applied.

clicksChange.description: Projected change in number of clicks if this option is applied.

impressionsChange.description: Projected change in number of impressions if this option is applied.

isRecommended.description: `true` if this is the primary recommended option. Only one option within a `RecommendedValueImpact` will have `isRecommended: true`.

X-Current-Token-Count.description: The number of API call tokens remaining in the current rate limit window.

X-Next-Replenishment-Time.description: The time (in epoch milliseconds) when the next batch of tokens will be replenished. Wait until this time before retrying.

authorization.name: Authorization
authorization.description: Basic authorization header. Base 64 encodes the Client ID and Client Secret retrieved in step two of the integration steps.

accessToken.name: WM_SEC.ACCESS_TOKEN
accessToken.description: Access token obtained from the Token API. This is required for authenticating requests to Walmart Marketplace APIs.

channelType.name: WM_CONSUMER.CHANNEL.TYPE
channelType.description: A unique ID to identify the consumer request by channel. Use the Consumer Channel Type received during onboarding.

correlationId.name: WM_QOS.CORRELATION_ID
correlationId.description: A unique ID that identifies each API call and is used to track and debug issues. Use a randomly generated GUID for this ID.

svcName.name: WM_SVC.NAME
svcName.description: Specifies the name of the Walmart service being called.
